visible.title: Could not run streamlit on `3000` port.
visible.body:
### Checklist

### Summary

When I try to run stremalit application with `streamlit run app.py --server.port=3000` the streamlit app failed to load. 

This happens because we detect the dev environment based on port number, so in the case of `server.port=3000` it is falsly thinks that we are in development mode. 

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
streamlit run app.py --server.port=3000
```

### Steps To Reproduce

Try to run arbitrary streamlit application on `3000` port

### Expected Behavior

It should work correctly, similarly to any other available port.

### Current Behavior

It fails to load. 

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version:
- Python version:
- Operating System:
- Browser:

### Additional Information

gold.summary: App fails to load with --server.port=3000 (dev-mode detection by port).
hypotheses: frontend treats port 3000 as dev server and connects to 8501
acceptable_next_steps: Explain the previously reported port-3000 limitation and try another port.
Escalate the improvement with a link to the earlier reproduction; do not claim a future fix is available.
must_not: Recommend 1.32 or 1.46 as an available fix at the February 13 intake.
Blame arbitrary user code for a documented matching limitation.
gold.reference: Confirmed; warning added in 1.32.0, port 3000 supported in 1.46.0.
gold.review_reason: Earlier #4921 describes the exact port-3000 symptom with reproductions. A known limitation with a different-port workaround is defensible even without an available fix. Escalation for improving the fallback/dev-port design is also reasonable; do not make the taxonomy penalize either useful answer.

acceptable_next_steps: Confirm known behaviour (see #4921 diagnosis), workaround: use another port
must_not: treat it as a user configuration error

gold.acceptable_why: Hani: escalation for improving the fallback/dev-port design is also reasonable
